subject: Career
title: Reciprocity Networks: The Favor Economy
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Reciprocity Networks: The Favor Economy.

hook.text: He helped the IT director with a presentation. Six months later, his team got priority on a critical system upgrade.

buildup.text: Organizations run on reciprocity. Favors create debts. Debts create leverage. This is the favor economy.

discovery.text: Wayne Baker's research shows the highest performers are those who give and receive favors most frequently.

twist.text: The favor economy requires trust. Transactional score-keeping ('I did X so you owe me Y') destroys it.

climax.text: Give generously without keeping score. The returns come unpredictably but reliably.

punchline.text: Favors aren't transactions. They're investments in relationship capital.

quiz.question: What did Wayne Baker's research find about workplace favors?
options: Highest performers give and receive favors most frequently

details.summary: Organizations run on an informal favor economy where people exchange help, information, and support outside formal job descriptions. Understanding and participating in this reciprocity network is essential for getting things done efficiently.
details.whyItMatters: Formal processes are often too slow for real-time organizational needs. The favor economy fills the gaps and accelerates results for those who invest in it.
takeaways: Small favors build trust credits that can be redeemed for larger requests
Always follow through on promises to maintain reciprocity credibility
Track your favor balance to avoid consistently over-drawing or under-giving

faq.question: How do you participate in the favor economy without being exploited?
faq.answer: Set boundaries by distinguishing between reasonable requests and chronic exploitation. Help generously but notice if the same person always asks without reciprocating. It is acceptable to gently redirect serial takers toward formal channels.

faq.question: Is the favor economy fair to people who are new to an organization?
faq.answer: New employees start with zero favor capital, which can be challenging. However, newcomers can build capital quickly by proactively offering help and being exceptionally reliable on small commitments. Early generosity compounds into a strong reciprocity network within months.
